clue.text: Anticipatory point, I see, said to follow one of the people

parts.note: a prole is one of the common people, the proletariat

indicators.note: said tells us the words I see are to be spoken, giving the sound of two letters

parts.note: the words I see, spoken, sound like the names of two letters

explanation.surface: Someone explains a point, says 'I see', and waits to follow a member of the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' only sets the order; 'said' turns the words 'I see' into the two letters they sound like.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolepsis is anticipation, so a proleptic figure of speech or argument is anticipatory.

clue.text: Peninsular and Albert? A beast!
